description: Recorded tool-call script for ECII Test A (an accessory for an existing system), replayed by the FAKE provider. It proves the structure only: the intent record, the deterministic gaps and the clarification question travel through the real operations, previews, Apply and the Conceptualize service. It is not a model run and says nothing about whether a model interprets such a request well; that is a live evaluation. Domain words appear here as fixture values only.

turns.user: ^Design a drill-bit holder that attaches to my cordless drill

arguments.rationale: The holder attaches to the person's own cordless drill, so it works with an existing system whose model is not stated.

externalSystems.name: Cordless drill (make and model not stated)
externalSystems.description: The person's cordless drill; the request does not say which model it is.

objectives: Keep drill bits within reach on the drill

questions.text: Which cordless drill model should the holder attach to?
questions.why: The attachment features differ between models and cannot be guessed; a wrong assumption would give a holder that does not fit.
options: Continue with a generic holder and decide the attachment later
Tell me the drill make and model so I can identify the mounting features
Upload photos or CAD of the drill
Supply measurements of the mounting features

arguments.reason: ECII Test A: interpret the intent before designing

steps.final: I interpreted this as an accessory that integrates with your cordless drill; the drill is not identified yet. Apply the intent to record it. I have not designed anything: I will list the information gaps and ask for the drill model first.

arguments.text: Ways the holder could attach to a drill whose model is not yet known
arguments.name: Holder mounting architectures

alternatives.name: Reuse the existing accessory fastener
alternatives.summary: The holder is clamped under a fastener the drill already has for accessories.

architecture.hostInterface: An existing accessory fastener location on the drill, if the model has one
architecture.interfaceGeometry: Fastener thread, boss position and spacing are not known for this model
risks: The fastener may loosen under vibration
assumptions: The drill has such a fastener (unverified)
architecture.attachmentPrinciple: Holder body clamped under the head of an existing fastener
architecture.loadPath: Weight of the holder and its contents goes into the fastener boss in shear
architecture.installationRemoval: Remove the fastener, place the holder, refasten
evidenceRequired: Drill model and the position and thread of the fastener

alternatives.name: Clamp around a housing feature
alternatives.summary: A split clamp closes around a cylindrical or prismatic part of the drill housing.

architecture.hostInterface: An outer housing section that a clamp can encircle
architecture.interfaceGeometry: Section size, shape and surface finish are not known for this model
advantages: Needs no fastener or slot on the drill
risks: A suitable section may not exist on this model
architecture.attachmentPrinciple: Friction clamp tightened around the housing section
architecture.loadPath: Clamping friction carries the weight into the housing
architecture.installationRemoval: Open the clamp, slide it over the section, tighten; reverse to remove
disadvantages: Can slip under load or mark the housing
evidenceRequired: Photos or measurements of the housing sections

alternatives.name: Attach to an existing rail or slot
alternatives.summary: A tongue on the holder engages a rail or slot that the drill already has.

architecture.hostInterface: An existing rail, slot or accessory interface on the drill
architecture.interfaceGeometry: Rail profile and slot dimensions are not known for this model
assumptions: The drill has a rail or slot (unverified)
architecture.attachmentPrinciple: Sliding tongue engaging a rail or slot, locked with a detent
architecture.loadPath: Weight goes through the tongue flanks into the rail or slot
architecture.installationRemoval: Slide on and off along the rail; the detent releases by hand
disadvantages: Only works if the drill has the rail or slot
evidenceRequired: Drill model and the profile of the rail or slot

steps.final: I prepared three different ways the holder could attach to the drill: reuse an existing accessory fastener, clamp around a housing feature, or engage an existing rail or slot. Each one names the host feature it depends on and the evidence needed; none of them states a dimension of your drill. Apply to record them; they are provisional until the drill is identified.
